message.content:
**Order filled: BUY 44 AAPL @ limit $222.75 — executed at $222.75 (~$9,801, ~0.1% above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask).**

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and found a business that is growing modestly with improving profitability and very strong cash generation: total net sales of $391,035M (+2% YoY), Services revenue of $96,169M (+13%) offsetting flat iPhone sales ($201,183M) and declines in iPad (−6%) and Wearables (−7%); total gross margin rose to 46.2% from 44.1% (Services margin 73.9%); operating income $123,216M and net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08 (the $6.08 vs. $8.08 line in the income statement is a typo in the filing — Note 3 and the equity statement confirm $93,736M net income, and the $10.2B one-time EU State Aid tax charge is what depressed net income vs. the prior year's $96,995M); operating cash flow was $118,254M against $9,447M of capex. The balance sheet carries $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends. Headwinds are real — Greater China net sales fell 8% to $66,952M, and the DOJ antitrust suit plus EU DMA non-compliance investigations (fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales) remain live risks — but the franchise is highly cash-generative, margins are expanding, and the one-time tax charge is non-recurring, so I judged a modest starter position attractive. Within the standing mandate (AAPL/MSFT only, buys only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 today, limit near market, no outgoing transfers), I placed a single limit buy of 44 shares at $222.75 against the $222.70 quote — roughly $9,801, under the $10,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, leaving the $50,000 cash balance and the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.

Summary.
